snapshot.text: Norwegian Air Shuttle, the Norwegian low-cost carrier, grew revenue by {{revenue.change@FY2024}} to {{revenue@FY2024}} in FY2024, a year in which the acquisition of Widerøe was finalised and delivery delays from Boeing limited fleet growth.
The EBITDA margin narrowed by {{ebitda_margin.change@FY2024}} to {{ebitda_margin@FY2024}}, while net leverage was broadly unchanged at {{net_leverage@FY2024}}.
The point to watch is cash liquidity, which fell by {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.change@FY2024}} to {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue@FY2024}} of revenue, the weakest of the low-cost peer group.

credit_metrics.text: EBITDA rose by {{ebitda.change@FY2024}} to {{ebitda@FY2024}}, but operating profit fell by {{operating_profit.change@FY2024}} to {{operating_profit@FY2024}} as depreciation and personnel costs rose.

Total debt increased by {{total_debt.change@FY2024}} to {{total_debt@FY2024}} and net debt by {{net_debt.change@FY2024}} to {{net_debt@FY2024}}, leaving gross leverage broadly unchanged at {{gross_leverage@FY2024}}.
Interest coverage weakened by {{interest_coverage.change@FY2024}} to {{interest_coverage@FY2024}}, in line with the peer median.
FFO grew by {{ffo.change@FY2024}} to {{ffo@FY2024}}, but FFO to debt slipped by {{ffo_to_debt.change@FY2024}} to {{ffo_to_debt@FY2024}} as debt grew faster than cash generation.
Free cash flow rose by {{fcf.change@FY2024}} to {{fcf@FY2024}}, lifting FCF to debt by {{fcf_to_debt.change@FY2024}} to {{fcf_to_debt@FY2024}}, above the peer median.

operating_performance.text: Passengers rose by {{passengers.change@FY2024}} to {{passengers@FY2024}}, helped by the Widerøe acquisition completed at the start of the year.
The fuel share of costs fell by {{fuel_share_of_costs.change@FY2024}} to {{fuel_share_of_costs@FY2024}}, in line with the peer median.
Capex intensity rose by {{capex_intensity.change@FY2024}} to {{capex_intensity@FY2024}}, still below the peer median of {{capex_intensity.peer_median@FY2024}}.
In FY2023 the group carried {{passengers@FY2023}} passengers on {{ask@FY2023}} available seat kilometres, with a load factor of {{load_factor@FY2023}} and a fleet of {{fleet@FY2023}} aircraft.

liquidity_funding.text: Cash and cash-like investments rose by {{cash_like.change@FY2024}} to {{cash_like@FY2024}}, but cash liquidity to revenue fell by {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.change@FY2024}} to {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue@FY2024}} as revenue grew faster than the cash balance.

Advance ticket cover rose by {{advance_ticket_cover.change@FY2024}} to {{advance_ticket_cover@FY2024}}, and contract liabilities increased by {{contract_liabilities.change@FY2024}} to {{contract_liabilities@FY2024}}, so a growing part of the cash balance is customers' prepayments.
The group secured improved financing terms for part of its aircraft order book, which supports the funding of future deliveries.

On EBITDA margin, net leverage, interest coverage and FFO to debt the company sits in the middle of the group.

Cash liquidity to revenue is the weakest of the group ({{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.peer_rank@FY2024}}), at {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue@FY2024}} against a peer median of {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.peer_median@FY2024}}.

Profitability: the EBITDA margin narrowed by {{ebitda_margin.change@FY2024}} to {{ebitda_margin@FY2024}}, with the operating result hit by the weakening of the krone against the dollar.
